'''Austin Jahn Green''' (born September 27, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa Panthers]].

==Early life==
Green attended Holmes Junior High School, where he first decided he wanted to play college basketball.<ref name="potter"/> He played for [[Cedar Falls High School]] on the basketball team as well as the Iowa Barnstormers in AAU play.<ref>{{cite news |last=Southard |first=Dargan |title=Inside top-100 guard AJ Green's unique recruiting process |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2017/07/13/look-inside-cedar-falls-guard-aj-greens-unique-recruiting-process/472815001/ |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=July 13, 2017}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 26 points per game and became Cedar Falls' all-time leading scorer. He led the team to a state championship.<ref name="southard"/>

===Recruiting===
Green was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the No. 78 player in the 2018 class by [[ESPN]]. On August 11, 2017, he committed to play college basketball for [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa]], where his father was a member of the coaching staff. Green became the highest-rated player to ever commit to Northern Iowa and the program's first four-star recruit.<ref name="southard">{{cite web |last=Southard |first=Dargan |title=AJ Green ready to handle hype, expectations ahead of freshman season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2018/10/17/northern-iowa-panthers-basketball-aj-green-ben-jacobson/1669935002/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |access-date=February 7, 2020 |date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> He chose the Panthers over Power 5 offers from [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web | title=AJ Green Recruit Interests | website=247Sports | url=https://247sports.com/recruitment/aj-green-99467/recruitinterests/ | access-date=2025-06-13}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Green averaged 15 points per game.<ref name="potter"/> However, he struggled with turnovers, with 77 assists to 94 turnovers.<ref>{{cite news |last=Petaros |first=Nick |title=UNI basketball: Battle-tested Panthers must embrace the fight |url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/uni/mens_basketball/uni-basketball-battle-tested-panthers-must-embrace-the-fight/article_7bd1b580-cbae-527c-92b4-526a172de09c.html |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier]] |date=October 18, 2019}}</ref> Green was named [[Missouri Valley Conference]] Freshman of the Year, becoming the first Northern Iowa player to receive the honor since [[Seth Tuttle]] in 2012, as well as Third Team All-MVC.<ref>{{cite news |last=Southard |first=Dargan |title=UNI basketball: AJ Green named Missouri Valley Conference freshman of the year |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2019/03/05/northern-iowa-panthers-mens-basketball-missouri-valley-conference-freshman-of-the-year-aj-green-uni/3069257002/ |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> On January 4, 2020, Green scored a career-high 35 points in a 69–64 win over [[2019–20 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Southard |first=Dargan |title='Appreciate what he's doing': UNI's AJ Green showcasing offensive prowess rarely seen in MVC |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2020/01/17/northern-iowa-panthers-uni-college-basketball-aj-green-missouri-valley-conference/4499783002/ |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=January 17, 2020}}</ref> He had 34 points on February 8, in an 83–73 win over [[2019–20 Drake Bulldogs men's basketball team|Drake]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Petaros |first=Nick |title=Green approaches 1,000-point milestone |url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/uni/mens_basketball/green-approaches--point-milestone/article_ac1bde77-af39-5dea-9613-dc2c101a3204.html |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier]] |date=February 11, 2020}}</ref> On February 12, Green scored 27 points in a 71–63 win over [[2019–20 Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball team|Illinois State]] and surpassed the 1,000-point threshold.<ref>{{cite news |last=Petaros |first=Nick |title=Northern Iowa's A.J. Green scores 1,000th point in win over Illinois State |url=https://siouxcityjournal.com/sports/college/northern-iowa-s-a-j-green-scores-th-point-in/article_ca75cd77-f8e5-5ceb-ae07-3aaba4676615.html |access-date=February 15, 2020 |work=[[Sioux City Journal]] |date=February 12, 2020}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season, Green was named MVC Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |last=Coleman |first=Rick |title=UNI's AJ Green wins MVC Player of the year |url=https://kwwl.com/2020/03/03/unis-green-wins-mvc-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=March 4, 2020 |work=KWWL |date=March 3, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 19.7 points and 3.0 assists per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gleeson |first=Scott |title=NCAA men's tournament primer: Everything you need to know to prepare for March Madness |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/03/02/college-basketball-march-madness-what-know-ncaa-tournament/4923937002/ |access-date=April 3, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 2, 2020}}</ref> Following the season, Green declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Southard |first=Dargan |title=UNI basketball: AJ Green declares for 2020 NBA Draft, leaves door open for college return |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2020/04/25/uni-basketball-a-j-green-declares-2020-nba-draft-not-hire-agent-maintain-eligibility-northern-iowa/3027806001/ |access-date=May 1, 2020 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=April 25, 2020}}</ref> However, on July 30, 2020, he withdrew from the draft and decided to return to Northern Iowa for his junior season.<ref>{{cite news|title=AJ Green Withdraws From 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://unipanthers.com/news/2020/7/30/mens-basketball-aj-green-withdraws-from-2020-nba-draft.aspx |access-date=January 2, 2021 |work=UNIPanthers.com|date=July 30, 2020}}</ref>

On December 13, 2020, Panthers head coach [[Ben Jacobson]] announced that Green would undergo hip surgery and miss the remainder of the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]]. He only appeared in 3 games, averaging 22.3 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bain |first=Matthew |title=UNI point guard AJ Green will undergo season-ending hip surgery|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2020/12/13/uni-point-guard-aj-green-undergo-season-ending-hip-surgery/6531266002/ |access-date=January 2, 2021 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=December 13, 2020}}</ref> The following season, Green returned and averaged 18.8 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game, culminating in his second selection as MVC Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://mvc-sports.com/news/2022/2/28/arch-madness-aj-green-of-uni-headlines-2022-mvc-mbb-all-conference-teams.aspx |title=AJ Green of UNI Headlines 2022 MVC MBB All-Conference Teams|publisher=[[Missouri Valley Conference]] |date=March 1, 2022 |access-date=March 1, 2022}}</ref> On April 20, 2022, Green entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] while also declaring for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and maintaining his college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pisani|first=Hart|url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/uni/mens_basketball/aj-green-declares-for-nba-draft-enters-portal/article_ec13524d-7335-5d1b-a118-480f83f5c1c1.html|title=AJ Green declares for NBA Draft, enters portal|work=[[The Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier]]|date=April 20, 2022}}</ref> However, on June 1, 2022, he announced he would remain in the draft and forego his remaining eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bair |first=Cole |title=UNI standout AJ Green to remain in 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://www.thegazette.com/panther-basketball/uni-standout-aj-green-to-remain-in-2022-nba-draft/|website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=June 1, 2022 |date=June 1, 2022}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2022–present) ===
After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Green signed a two-way contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign AJ Green to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-aj-green-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=July 1, 2022}}</ref> Green joined the Bucks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612749/bucks|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2022}}</ref> In his Summer League debut, Green scored fourteen points in a 94–90 win against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets vs Milwaukee Bucks Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bkn-vs-mil-1522200006/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2022}}</ref>

On July 7, 2023, Green signed a standard contract with the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Re-Sign AJ Green|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-aj-green|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> The contract was for three years and $6.3 million, including $1.9 million guaranteed at signing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AJ Green {{!}} NBA Contracts & Salaries |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/player/_/id/78250/aj-green/contract/summary |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=spotrac.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 9, 2024, Green scored a career-high 27 points during a 125–109 loss to the [[2023–24 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2024 |title=Former UNI Panther AJ Green scores NBA Career High 27 points for Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://www.kwwl.com/news/former-uni-panther-aj-green-scores-nba-career-high-27-points-for-milwaukee-bucks/article_c4c52d84-c7ac-11ee-bc84-b31660538517.html |access-date=May 1, 2024 |website=KWWL |language=en}}</ref>

Green made 73 appearances (seven starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.4 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. On April 29, 2025, during the first round of the playoffs, Green recorded 19 points and four rebounds in a 119–118 Game 5 overtime loss against the [[Indiana Pacers]], eliminating the Bucks from the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Haliburton and Pacers eliminate Bucks from playoffs, closing OT with 8-0 run to win 119-118 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768050 |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

On October 16, 2025, Green signed a four-year, $45 million contract extension with the Bucks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nehm |first=Eric |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Bucks, shooting guard AJ Green agree to 4-year, $45 million extension |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6723868/2025/10/16/bucks-aj-green-extension-nba/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign AJ Green To Multi-Year Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-aj-green-to-multi-year-contract-extension|date=October 17, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 17, 2025}}</ref>

On April 10, 2026, Green put a career-high 35 points on a career-high 11 three-pointers made in a 125–108 win over the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]]. His 11 three-pointers made set a record for the most three-pointers made in a game in Bucks franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/milwaukee-bucks/bucks-news-aj-green-passes-damian-lillard-milwaukee-history|title=AJ Green passes Damian Lillard in Bucks history|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=April 10, 2026|access-date=April 10, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2026/04/10/milwaukee-bucks-injury-report-giannis-antetokounmpo-last-home-game/89549497007/|title=AJ Green's record night helps Bucks close home slate with a victory|website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|last1=Owczarski|first1=Jim|last2=Steele|first2=Ben|date=April 10, 2026|access-date=April 10, 2026}}</ref> On April 12, Green put up 19 points with five three-pointers made in a 126–106 loss to the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]]. Green also surpassed [[Ray Allen]] (229) for the most three-pointers made in a season in Bucks franchise history with 232.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/milwaukee-bucks/bucks-aj-green-sets-new-franchise-record-amid-76ers-clash|title=Bucks’ AJ Green sets new franchise record amid 76ers clash|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2026/04/12/milwaukee-bucks-aj-green-ray-allen-record-philadelphia-76ers-live-updates/89558620007/|title=AJ Green sets 3-point record, 76ers beat Bucks 126-106|website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|last=Owczarski|first=Jim|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Green's father, Kyle Green, is a former associate head basketball coach for [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] and now the Head Coach for [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Birch | first=Tommy | title=Behind the scenes of how Iowa native AJ Green made it to the NBA | website=The Des Moines Register | date=2025-08-07 | url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/northern-iowa/uni-panthers/2025/08/07/aj-green-cedar-falls-northern-iowa-milwaukee-bucks-iowa-state-cyclones-kyle-green/85523605007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=undefined&gca-ft=0&gca-ds=sophi&gnt-djm=1 | access-date=2025-12-02}}</ref> He was previously an assistant coach and later associate head coach for [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa]]. Kyle played [[NCAA Division III]] basketball for [[Hamline University#Men's basketball|Hamline University]] before spending one season professionally in [[Denmark]], where he also began his coaching career.<ref name="potter">{{cite web |last=Potter |first=Jacob |title=Father-son bond– A.J. Green's dream to play under his dad |url=https://www.northerniowan.com/11758/sports/father-son-bond-a-j-greens-dream-to-play-under-his-dad/ |website=[[The Northern Iowan]] |access-date=February 7, 2020 |date=November 21, 2019}}</ref> Green's mother, Michele, played basketball for Hamline and is a [[chiropractor]]. Green's younger sister, Emerson, played basketball for [[Cedar Falls High School]] and is now playing at [[Northern Iowa Panthers women's basketball|Northern Iowa]].<ref name="bair">{{cite web |last=Bair |first=Cole |title=UNI's AJ Green has basketball in his blood |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/uni-panthers/unis-aj-green-has-basketball-in-his-blood-20191231 |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |access-date=February 7, 2020 |date=December 31, 2019}}</ref>
